effect: The fuelled mitochondria made an ATP supply, connecting fuel processing to the muscle’s pulling machinery.

reason: The filament-filled muscle fibre needs ATP for its pulling machinery.
expectation: The ATP supply will equip the fibre for pulling.

effect: ATP has prepared the fibre's myosin heads, but the covered binding site suggests a signal is still needed for pulling.
reaction: The picture makes ATP's role in releasing and resetting the heads more specific.
reason: The calcium signal is the available signal at the filaments and may uncover the binding sites.
expectation: Calcium will enable the filaments to interact and the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium enabled the fibre to shorten by allowing the filaments to slide past one another. The remaining goal is relaxation.
reaction: The distinction between the fibre shortening and the filaments themselves staying the same length is useful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes appear to remove calcium from around the filaments so the fibre can relax.
expectation: The pumps will return calcium to storage, allowing the muscle fibre to relax and prepare for another pull.

effect: Calcium pumps returned calcium to storage using ATP, stopping the pulling and completing the goal. Relaxation also requires cellular work.
reaction: The role of ATP in relaxation was a useful connection.

mostWorthwhile.text: The calcium signal producing a shortening fibre was most worthwhile: the description distinguishes the fibre shortening from the filaments sliding past one another, then connects that movement to calcium.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the filament units was straightforward but contributed less explanation than the later descriptions of how they move.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin release and reset, and calcium must then uncover the grip sites before pulling can occur. That made the roles of the two inputs more specific.
